class.name: CanvasPostProcess
class.brief_description: Applies post-processing effects to 2D canvas rendering.
class.description: CanvasPostProcess is a Control node that applies full-screen post-processing effects to the 2D canvas. It supports pixelation, chromatic aberration, gaussian blur, radial blur, color adjustment, scanlines, film grain, and vignette effects. Effects are processed in that order (matching the Inspector panel layout). Place this node in your scene tree to apply effects to all 2D content rendered before it. To exclude UI elements (e.g., dialog boxes, HUD) from post-processing, use a [SubViewport] to isolate the game content.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], enables the pixelation effect which reduces the effective resolution.
The size of each pixel block in the pixelation effect. Larger values produce a more pixelated appearance.
If [code]true[/code], enables chromatic aberration which shifts RGB channels apart, simulating lens distortion.
Controls the intensity of the chromatic aberration effect. Higher values produce more visible color fringing.
If [code]true[/code], enables the gaussian blur effect.
Controls the radius/strength of the blur. Higher values produce a more blurred image.
The number of blur iterations. More iterations produce a smoother blur but cost more performance.
If [code]true[/code], enables radial blur which blurs outward from a center point, creating a zoom/speed effect.
Controls the intensity of the radial blur. Higher values produce a stronger zoom blur.
The number of samples for radial blur. More samples produce smoother results but cost more performance.
The center point of the radial blur in UV coordinates (0.0 to 1.0). Default is the screen center.
If [code]true[/code], enables color adjustment (brightness, contrast, saturation).
Multiplier for the overall brightness. Values above 1.0 brighten the image, values below 1.0 darken it.
Controls the contrast. Values above 1.0 increase contrast, values below 1.0 reduce it.
Controls the color saturation. A value of 0.0 produces a grayscale image, values above 1.0 produce more vivid colors.
If [code]true[/code], enables the scanlines effect which overlays horizontal lines simulating a CRT display.
Controls the density (frequency) of the scanlines. Higher values produce thinner, more closely spaced lines.
Controls the opacity/visibility of the scanlines. Higher values make the lines more pronounced.
Controls the scrolling speed of the scanlines. A value of 0.0 keeps them static.
If [code]true[/code], enables the film grain effect which adds random noise to simulate a cinematic look.
Controls the intensity of the film grain noise. Higher values produce more visible grain.
Controls how fast the grain pattern changes. Higher values produce more rapid flickering.
If [code]true[/code], enables the vignette effect which darkens the edges of the screen.
Controls how far the vignette extends from the edges toward the center. Higher values produce a larger darkened area.
Controls the softness of the vignette transition. Higher values produce a smoother gradient.
The color used for the vignette effect. The alpha channel controls the overall vignette opacity.
